chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Hasan from Zur'ah from Sama'ah said:

I asked him about combining Maghrib and the last 'Isha with a single combination (jam' taqdim or jam' ta'khir), so he said: 'Do not pray them until you reach the combination, even if part of the night has passed, for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) combined them with one Adhan and two Iqamas, just as he combined Dhuhr and 'Asr at 'Arafat.'

key_terms.اَلْجَمْعُ: Combining two prayers in one time
key_terms.عَرَفَاتٍ: Arafat, the plain where the Prophet combined Dhuhr and 'Asr

ai.seo_question: How should Maghrib and 'Isha prayers be combined during Hajj at Muzdalifah?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the specific method of *Jam' Taqdim* (early combination) for Maghrib and 'Isha at Muzdalifah, emphasizing that the combination is valid even if delayed until late night, provided the intention is to combine. It draws a direct parallel to the Prophet’s practice at 'Arafat, establishing a consistent jurisprudential model for combining prayers during Hajj rituals through a single Adhan and two Iqamas. This ruling underscores the flexibility within Shia fiqh regarding prayer times during pilgrimage, prioritizing the ritual context over strict temporal boundaries.
